newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares drop slightly on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares drop slightly on profit taking.

text.p: Jakarta share prices dropped slightly at the close of trade on Wednesday as some investors took late profits after earlier gains, brokers said.

They said weak regional markets also contributed to the lower index. "The market is already feeling the holiday-mood. Investors are just trading on a short-term basis because the buying season for some foreign investors has finished," a broker with London-based securities house said.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Thursday as sentiment was relatively weak.

The Jakarta Composite Index fell 0.10 points, or 0.02 percent, to close at 626.57 points after a high of 632.63 points. Losers led gainers by 53 to 46, with 67 counters steady. Total volume was 579.5 million shares on a turnover of 1.8 trillion rupiah.

Brokers said it was boosted by the cross-trade transactions of Telkom on a volume of 389.1 million shares combined with the listing of Bank Umum Servitia. Telkom fell 25 rupiah to 3,850 rupiah on a volume of 9.5 million shares after an earlier high of 4,075 rupiah.

They said investors were buying back shares after the government said it was making a block sale of 388 million shares and this pushed the price to a high of 4,075 before it eased slightly on profit taking.

On Wednesday, Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said the government was making a block sale in the state telecommunications giant Telkom to raise $600 million to accelerate payements on high-interest foreign debt.

Secondary Bank Umum Servitia, listed on Wednesday, topped the active list with 28.9 million shares changing hands at a price of 1,125 rupiah. It had an early peak at 1,175 rupiah before easing to 1,150 rupiah, up from its offer price of 800 rupiah.
Brokers said locally-led active buying of the stock gave a boost to overall market sentiment.
Another telecommunications stock Indosat rose 125 rupiah to 6,350 rupiah on a volume of 1.6 million shares on what brokers described as bargain-hunting.
"Some overseas buyers were buying actively on perception that the prevailing price was cheap," a foreign broker said.
